actions.description: The declared re-enable after a safety reset: publish a zero Twist on /cmd_vel, then unpause the world with a WorldControl request (pause false) on /world/default/control. DiffDrive keeps the last Twist it received and applies it as soon as the world runs; the zero replaces it, but it is an unacknowledged publication, so a stored command can still act for a few world steps.

device.model: TortoiseBot differential-drive robot in Ignition Fortress
device.name: TortoiseBot Ignition simulation environment

facts.text: The ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge declares /cmd_vel as geometry_msgs/msg/Twist in the ROS to Ignition direction, /odom as nav_msgs/msg/Odometry and /clock as rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock in the Ignition to ROS direction.
The launch script binds the scan endpoint name /scan.
The ros_gz_bridge declares the scan bridge as sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan.
The Ignition DiffDrive system plugin takes its commands from the /cmd_vel topic and names /odom as its odometry topic.
The Ignition DiffDrive system names frame_id odom and child_frame_id base_link.
The DiffDrive system declares max_linear_velocity 0.23 and min_linear_velocity -0.23 m/s.
The DiffDrive system declares max_angular_velocity 1.5 and min_angular_velocity -1.5 rad/s.
The DiffDrive system configures wheel_separation 0.17186 m and wheel_radius 0.0325 m.
The DiffDrive system publishes odometry at 50 Hz.
The gpu_lidar sensor ydlidar has update_rate 10.0 and topic /scan.
The gpu_lidar sensor publishes 360 horizontal samples between -3.14159 and 3.14159 rad with a 0.3 to 12.0 m range and 0.01 m resolution.
The README states that TortoiseBot uses Ignition Fortress as its simulation backend.
The real-robot firmware script differential.py imports RPi.GPIO and defines the motor enable and direction pins.
The Differential node subscribes Twist on cmd_vel and publishes lpwm, rpwm, ldir and rdir.
The Differential callback computes the wheel velocities from linear.x and angular.z and calls stop when both are zero, otherwise wheel_vel_executer.
autobringup.launch.py starts tortoisebot_firmware's differential.py as node differential unless use_sim_time is set.
The Ignition launch's default world is worlds/nav2_test_world.sdf.
nav2_test_world.sdf names its world default.
room2.sdf names its world default.
The launch's joint-state bridge reads /world/default/model/tortoisebot/joint_state.
The launch runs ign gazebo -r with the GUI when gui is true and with -s when it is false.
The launch's main bridge sets QoS overrides for its /tf_static, /scan and /odom publishers.
The README names ROS 2 Humble.
SimulationRunner composes its transport namespace as /world/ followed by the world name.
SimulationRunner advertises the control service with OnWorldControl as its callback.
OnWorldControl copies the WorldControl request into a WorldControlState and calls OnWorldControlState.
OnWorldControlState appends the control to worldControls and sets the Boolean reply to true.
ProcessWorldControl calls SetPaused with the pause flag of each queued control.
A queued control with multi_step on a paused world adds the steps and unpauses the world so that stepping can occur.
SetPaused stores the pause state in currentInfo.paused.
Step publishes the world statistics.
Step processes the world control messages.
The Run loop calls Step on every iteration and counts a processed iteration only while not paused.
The statistics publisher on the stats topic is limited to 10 messages per second.
PublishStats copies currentInfo.paused into the WorldStatistics message.
UpdateCurrentInfo advances the simulation time and the iteration count only while not paused.
The Physics system steps the physics only when not paused.
DiffDrive's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
DiffDrive's PostUpdate returns early while paused.
DiffDrive's cmd_vel callback stores the received Twist as its target velocity while enabled.
The bridge maps ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld to an ignition.msgs.WorldControl request with an ignition.msgs.Boolean reply.
The ControlWorld response's success is the Boolean reply's data.
For a failed request the ControlWorld response's success is false.
The service bridge converts each ROS request and sends it with Request and a callback that sends the ROS response.
The WorldStatistics conversion copies the Ignition header into the ROS header and copies paused.
ros_gz_interfaces WorldStatistics carries a header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and the paused flag.
ControlWorld takes a WorldControl request and answers bool success.
WorldControl's fields include pause, step and multi_step.
The bridge README maps ros_gz_interfaces/msg/WorldStatistics to ignition.msgs.WorldStatistics.
The bridge README maps the ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld service to ignition.msgs.WorldControl and ignition.msgs.Boolean.
The bridge README's service example starts parameter_bridge with a /world/<name>/control ControlWorld argument.
The bridge's publisher QoS is KeepLast with the queue size, and its depth, durability, history and reliability may be overridden.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned topic replies with no Ignition physics, DiffDrive integration, lidar raycast or state-hash replay; its world statistics follow the wall clock

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic: it answers the declared subscriptions and services and records the declared publication, but runs no Ignition Gazebo, ros_gz_bridge, physics, DiffDrive system, sensor model or ROS graph

the /odom pose and twist, /clock time and /scan ranges are placeholders; the fake returns an 8-element placeholder scan array while the pinned gpu_lidar sensor declares 360 samples (tortoisebot_gazebo/gazebo/tortoisebot_ignition.gazebo:90-99)
one subscription reply is not the pinned 50 Hz odometry or 10 Hz scan stream; no timing, drop or QoS behaviour of those streams is modeled
the camera stream /camera/image_raw, the TF tree, Nav2, AMCL and Cartographer are outside this package and are not covered

the binding cannot tell the simulation from the real robot: autobringup.launch.py:76-82 starts differential.py, which drives the Raspberry Pi GPIO motors from the same cmd_vel topic (differential.py:102-130), so a rosbridge endpoint on a real TortoiseBot moves the real base, where no world exists and the e-stop fails closed
the bridge refuses non-finite numbers, so a scan whose ranges contain inf or NaN (for example a beam without a return) fails the read without output instead of being served as data

the stop is the companion Ignition world pause (WorldControl through ros_gz ControlWorld), whose reply is true for any request the simulator queued (SimulationRunner.cc:1174-1176); it is confirmed by the E2 read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that the control request sets after its next statistics sample and publishes /world/default/stats every 100 ms (placeholder) while subscribed; it runs no SimulationRunner

the e-stop endpoints exist only while the operator runs ros_gz's parameter_bridge with the two arguments of operator_bridges (the clone's bridges carry topics only, ignition_sim.launch.py:69-109); without them the control call is not answered and the read-back sees no sample, so the e-stop fails closed; the declared estop_latency_ms 1500 covers the control call (400 ms) and the read-back bound (600 ms)

the read-back's freshness is the arrival time only: the bridged WorldStatistics header is the Ignition header, which PublishStats does not stamp (ros_gz convert copies it, ros_gz_interfaces.cpp:823); the bridge's publisher QoS sets only KeepLast with the queue size (factory.hpp:60-80), so its durability stays rclcpp's default, volatile, which replays no history to a late subscriber; the first sample is discarded and a burst of samples restarts the count; a QoS override of the stats publisher to a deeper transient-local history (the clone's own bridge overrides other publishers, ignition_sim.launch.py:86-91) is not covered beyond that burst rule

the endpoints name the world default, the name of both shipped worlds (nav2_test_world.sdf:4, room2.sdf:2) that the clone itself composes (ignition_sim.launch.py:99-102); a world with another name has other endpoints, and the e-stop fails closed

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Ignition GUI that the launch starts when gui is true (ignition_sim.launch.py:111-115), a WorldControl multi_step (SimulationRunner.cc:1244-1251) or any client of the control service; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

while paused, DiffDrive does not publish /odom (DiffDrive.cc:518-520) and sensors update on simulation time, which a paused world does not advance (SimulationRunner.cc:345-350); the fake silences /odom and /scan while paused, their reads fail NOT_READY after their timeouts, and the device resource reads no topic; /clock keeps the frozen time

the resume publishes a zero Twist before the unpause: DiffDrive keeps the last Twist (DiffDrive.cc:654-661) and the bridge forwards /cmd_vel while paused; the zero is unacknowledged and the simulation launch has no command timeout; the teleop keyboard and firmware/scripts/1ms.py also publish cmd_vel; the world resumes from the state it paused in, body velocities included
the deployment's ignition-gazebo and ros_gz must be the pinned 6.18.0 and 0.244.27 releases (ROS 2 Humble with Ignition Fortress); rosbridge cannot read the versions

The world statistics, whose paused flag confirms the e-stop.

safe_state.description: The world default is paused: after the WorldControl pause two fresh stats samples, 40 ms or more apart within 600 ms, reported paused true, so the world does not step and DiffDrive applies no velocity; it is the paused flag in that window, not a measured standstill, it needs the operator-run ros_gz bridges, and the GUI, a WorldControl client or a step request can unpause or step the world.
